items.description:
Did you know that Vikings captured people and sold them into slavery?

The Vikings didn't just steal treasure — they captured and traded human beings.

Captives taken during raids in the British Isles and Eastern Europe could be sold at trading centres including Hedeby and Bolghar, or forced to work as thralls. Viking-era slavery is documented in written sources and archaeology.

items.title: One Pig Nearly Started a War 😳 | The Pig War of 1859
items.description:

In 1859, American settler Lyman Cutlar shot a Hudson’s Bay Company pig rooting in his garden on disputed San Juan Island. British arrest threats triggered an armed standoff. U.S. troops and British warships faced each other—but officers refused to fire. The boundary dispute was later resolved peacefully.

items.title: The Blood Eagle: Real Viking Execution or Dark Legend? 😳
items.description:
Was the Blood Eagle a real Viking execution — or a terrifying story written down centuries later?

Medieval Norse and Latin accounts describe a ritual supposedly inflicted on powerful enemies. Historians debate whether these texts record an actual Viking Age practice or literary elaboration. A 2022 peer-reviewed study found the described ritual physically possible, but did NOT establish that it actually occurred.

The footage is a non-graphic, AI-generated historical reconstruction, not evidence of the ritual.

Source: Murphy, Fuller, Willan & Gates, “An Anatomy of the Blood Eagle: The Practicalities of Viking Torture,” Speculum (2022), https://doi.org/10.1086/717332

items.title: The Day Vikings Attacked God's Island 😱 | 793
items.description:
On 8 June 793, Viking raiders attacked the island monastery of Lindisfarne in Northumbria. It wasn't England's first Viking raid, and the Christian community at Lindisfarne survived.
